title: Minimax Rates for Incremental Survival Contrasts with Growing Odds Multipliers and Horizons
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope; paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.4.
gap_reasons: Its contribution is nevertheless confined to a deliberately engineered scalar-uniform experiment with fixed known treatment and censoring mechanisms, a quadratic joint corner, and fixed Lipschitz hazards; it does not establish the same frontier for estimated mechanisms or a conventional observational model.

The practical case is consequently limited by the absence of numerical evidence showing when the transported procedure improves on the raw score at usable sample sizes, an issue the note itself identifies but leaves unresolved.

The positioning review does not give relevance/comparison sentences for every cited work: in particular Sandqvist2024 and Tsybakov2009 appear in the bibliography/core but not in the substantive related-work account; add concise role-and-difference sentences (or remove citations not used).
proof_attempt_summary: The discovery run derived a matched four-region minimax and honest-length frontier for known treatment and censoring mechanisms; the mathematical referee passed it with no findings. D0.5.G rated the result subfield against a field floor because the experiment and practical evidence remain too narrow, and supplied no in-scope improvement directive. A later re-anchor would need substantive estimated-mechanism or observational results and should also repair the outstanding Sandqvist/Tsybakov comparison sentences.
tldr: For every fixed known treatment and censoring mechanism in the stated product-envelope class, a continuous-time incremental survival contrast with odds multiplier \(n^{\lambda}\) and horizon \(1-n^{-\kappa}\) has minimax absolute error and minimax honest expected length \(r_n=n^{-1/2}/\sqrt{A_nD_n}\), where \(A_n=\max\{n^{-\lambda/2},(n d_n^3)^{-1/5}\}\), \(D_n=\max\{A_n,n^{-\kappa}\}\), and \(d_n=\max\{n^{-\kappa},n^{-1/8}\}\). An observable event score transports covariate mass by a time-dependent amount, while a legal tent-hazard direction in the complete observed-record likelihood supplies the converse. The field-tier contribution is the matched four-region moving-policy frontier, including rate \(n^{-3/8}\) at \((1/3,1/6)\) and \((1/4,1/8)\) with no transition logarithm; it is not a generic unknown-mechanism observational-inference guarantee.
gap: Choi2026IncrementalSurvival gives fixed bounded-multiplier survival surfaces with nonparametric bootstrap bands, SchindlShenKennedy2026Continuous gives an \(n/\delta\) effective-sample-size law without right censoring, and the banked fixed-policy RMST frontier has no moving intervention scale. None characterizes the joint information loss caused by a growing binary-treatment odds shift and a horizon approaching a covariate-dependent censoring endpoint.
fill: The paper will give an explicit observable estimator, finite-sample honest interval, complete observed-likelihood converse, theorem-level reductions to each closest comparator, and a closed four-region moving-policy phase diagram over the full fixed exponent rectangle.
